judged_text: When credential sharing is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response object, but googlecalendar expects {res: {data}} (reads res?.data then token.access_token), hubspot expects a HubspotToken, and zoho/zoho-bigin expect an axios response (read tokenInfo.data.error), so the sync path structurally cannot satisfy any of these callers. With APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED on, every token refresh on the Google path throws TypeError reading .access_token of undefined, Hubspot reads accessToken off a Response (undefined), and zoho-bigin/zohocrm throw TypeError on tokenInfo.data.error — every shared-mode calendar refresh crashes instead of returning a token, so booking flows that depend on these integrations fail. Additionally the sync endpoint's response.ok is never checked, so a 401/500 from the sync service is handed to callers as if it were a token response.

adjudication.rationale: In shared mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`), `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch(...)` Response (`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`) instead of the shape expected by multiple callers. For example, Google Calendar assigns `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then does `const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token` (`packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`), but a `Response` has no `.data`, so `token` becomes `undefined` and `token.access_token` will throw. Zoho Bigin/Zoho CRM expect an axios response and access `tokenInfo.data...` (`packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts`), which will also throw with a `Response`. Hubspot similarly expects a `HubspotToken` object but may receive a `Response` (`packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`). Additionally, the shared-mode path never checks `response.ok`, so non-2xx responses are passed through as if valid token refresh results.
